newsitem.title: INDIA: India Basmati rice prices surge on European demand.
newsitem.headline: India Basmati rice prices surge on European demand.

text.p: Indian aromatic Basmati rice prices firmed by about $200 per tonne in the past week due to a surge in demand from European and Middle East countries and a lower crop forecast, traders said on Thursday.

"Prices had risen by $200 per tonne because of increased demand from Europe and the Middle East countries and lower crop expectation," said Prem Garg, managing director of Sri Lal Mahal Overseas Ltd, a leading Delhi foodgrains exporter.
"Basmati prices are high as international demand is more and there is a shortfall in the crop," said Deepak Tanna, a leading Bombay foodgrains exporter.
Traders said Basmati was currently quoted at around $1,200 per tonne FOB compared with $1,000 a week earlier.
Tanna said the 1996/97 (July/June) Basmati crop was expected to be less than the previous year but did not say by how much.
India produced a little more than 600,000 tonnes of Basmati in 1995/96.
Traders said export demand for Indian non-Basmati rice was dull as it was quoted about $20-$30 per tonne higher than that of similar grades from Pakistan and Vietnam.
"The (export) demand is not very much there," Tanna said.
Garg said: "Some parboiled rice and five percent broken grades are going to South Africa and the Middle East."
Traders said Indian five percent broken non-Basmati rice was quoted at $300 per tonne FOB, 10 percent at $280-285, 15 percent at $250-255 and 25 percent at $235-240 per tonne.
